critical.claim: VAT on pre-incorporation purchases is permanently lost/unreclaimable whenever the supplier's invoice is in the founder's personal name, with the only escape being a narrow 'acting as agent' exception (or asking the supplier to credit-note and re-invoice the company).
critical.postQuote: The general rule is that a company can only reclaim VAT on supplies made to it. If the invoice is addressed to you as an individual, the company cannot reclaim the VAT, even if the goods are used by the company after incorporation. There is a narrow exception. If the goods were acquired by the individual as agent for the company ... HMRC may allow the claim.
critical.location: body, section 'The VAT Trap: Pre-Incorporation Input Tax' (also repeated in metaDescription, summary, and FAQ 'Can I reclaim VAT on purchases made before my company was registered?')
critical.whatsWrong: This inverts HMRC's actual published position. Under Regulation 111 of the VAT Regulations 1995 (HMRC manual VIT32000), a newly incorporated, VAT-registered company CAN recover pre-incorporation input VAT even where the supply was made to a person who later became a director/employee/shareholder, provided the company pays for (or undertakes to pay for) the cost (typically via the director's loan account) and the supply relates to the company's taxable business. The 'agent' route is not the main mechanism; the standard Regulation 111 route is. Time limits are 4 years for goods still on hand and 6 months for services before registration. The article tells readers this VAT is a 'permanent cost', which is the opposite of the law and would cause them to forgo a legitimate, sizeable reclaim.
critical.correctValue: Pre-incorporation input VAT is generally RECOVERABLE by the company under VAT Regulations 1995 reg.111 / HMRC VIT32000: goods still on hand within 4 years and services within 6 months of registration, where the company pays for the supply (e.g. via director's loan account) and it relates to the company's taxable activities, even though the invoice is in the founder's personal name.
critical.fix: Rewrite the VAT section (and metaDescription, summary, FAQ) to state that pre-incorporation VAT is normally reclaimable under VAT Regulations 1995 reg.111 (4-year goods / 6-month services limits) where the company pays for the supply via the director's loan account, citing HMRC VIT32000; remove the 'permanent cost' / 'cannot reclaim' framing.
